cards.ex: The feeling of being happy with what you have or what you have achieved.

cards.note: status 是别人眼中的相对位置；不是财富数量。

cards.ex: To matter means to be important.

cards.ex: Hunter-gatherers were early humans who lived by hunting animals and collecting plants.
exs: Hunter-gatherers moved often to find food.
We still have hunter-gatherer brains.

src.t: In old society, let’s go back to hunter-gatherer times, there was no such thing as wealth – you just had what you could carry.
src.zh: 回到很久以前的狩猎采集时代，那时候还谈不上我们今天理解的那种财富——你能拥有的，基本就是自己带得走的东西。

lg: 拿弓打猎、伸手摘果的原始人。

cards.ex: There's no such thing as X means X does not exist.
exs: There's no such thing as a free lunch.
There's no such thing as a perfect lash set.

src.t: In old society, let’s go back to hunter-gatherer times, there was no such thing as wealth – you just had what you could carry.

cards.ex: Money, property, and other valuable things that a person or group owns.
exs: She built her wealth slowly.
Health is more important than wealth.

src.t: In old society, let’s go back to hunter-gatherer times, there was no such thing as wealth – you just had what you could carry.
src.zh: 回到很久以前的狩猎采集时代，那时候还谈不上我们今天理解的那种财富——你能拥有的，基本就是自己带得走的东西。

cards.ex: Stored means kept somewhere so you can use it later.
exs: Stored food lasts the winter.
My stored photos take up a lot of space.

src.t: There was no stored wealth, so wealth creation games didn’t exist.
src.zh: 当时没有多少能长期储存的财富，所以也谈不上通过创造财富来竞争。

cards.ex: Making new value through useful products, services, or other work.
exs: Small businesses drive wealth creation.
Wealth creation isn't zero-sum.

src.t: There was no stored wealth, so wealth creation games didn’t exist.
src.zh: 当时没有多少能长期储存的财富，所以也谈不上通过创造财富来竞争。

cards.note: 创造新的价值 ≠ 仅把现有的钱从别人那里拿过来。

cards.ex: To exist means to be real, to be there.
exs: Do ghosts exist?
Back then, phones didn't exist.

src.t: All that existed was status games.
src.zh: 存在的只有地位游戏。

cards.ex: Ready for someone to use, get, or choose; also free at a particular time.
exs: Is Friday available?
There was little food available.

src.t: If you were high status, then you got what little was available first, but even back then you had to earn your status by taking care of the tribe.
src.zh: 如果你地位高，就能先拿到那一点点可用的东西，但即使在那时，你也得靠照顾部落来赢得地位。

cards.ex: Back then means at that time in the past.
exs: Back then, I worked in a factory.
Life was simpler back then.

src.t: If you were high status, then you got what little was available first, but even back then you had to earn your status by taking care of the tribe.
src.zh: 如果你地位高，就能先拿到那一点点可用的东西，但即使在那时，你也得靠照顾部落来赢得地位。

cards.ex: A product is something that is made to be sold.
exs: This aftercare product is great.
She launched her own product line.

src.t: Now we have wealth creation where you can actually create a product or a service.
src.zh: 现在我们有了财富创造，你真的可以创造一个产品或一项服务。

cards.ex: A service is work you do for other people, often for money.
exs: Lash lifts are my most popular service.
The service here is excellent.

src.t: Now we have wealth creation where you can actually create a product or a service.
src.zh: 现在我们有了财富创造，你真的可以创造一个产品或一项服务。

cards.ex: To grow a business or service so it can serve more people without the work growing at the same rate.
exs: I want to scale my studio to three chairs.
Online courses scale easily.

src.t: You can scale that product or service and you can provide abundance for a lot of people, and that’s not zero-sum, that’s a positive-sum game.
src.zh: 你可以把产品或服务做大，让更多人受益。这不是零和游戏，而是大家都可能得到更多的正和游戏。

cards.note: scale 不只是变大，而是让产出增长得比投入更快；例如一个视频被很多人看到。

cards.ex: A large amount of something, often more than people need.
exs: There's an abundance of fresh fruit in summer.
Think in abundance, not scarcity.

src.t: You can scale that product or service and you can provide abundance for a lot of people, and that’s not zero-sum, that’s a positive-sum game.
src.zh: 你可以把产品或服务做大，让更多人受益。这不是零和游戏，而是大家都可能得到更多的正和游戏。

cards.ex: A situation where one person can gain only if someone else loses an equal amount.
exs: Friendship isn't a zero-sum game.
Rankings are zero-sum.

src.t: You can scale that product or service and you can provide abundance for a lot of people, and that’s not zero-sum, that’s a positive-sum game.
src.zh: 你可以把产品或服务做大，让更多人受益。这不是零和游戏，而是大家都可能得到更多的正和游戏。

cards.note: 一方多得一份，另一方就相对少一份；讲的是总量不增加的竞争。

cards.ex: A situation where people can create more total value, so more than one person can benefit.
exs: Good trade is positive-sum.
Teaching others is a positive-sum game.

src.t: You can scale that product or service and you can provide abundance for a lot of people, and that’s not zero-sum, that’s a positive-sum game.
src.zh: 你可以把产品或服务做大，让更多人受益。这不是零和游戏，而是大家都可能得到更多的正和游戏。

cards.note: 重点是总价值可以增加，不保证每个人每一次都获利。

cards.ex: Wealthy means having a lot of money.
exs: She comes from a wealthy family.
You don't have to be wealthy to be happy.

src.t: I can be wealthy, you can be wealthy, we can create things together.
src.zh: 我可以富有，你也可以富有，我们可以一起创造东西。

cards.ex: Collectively means as a group, all together.
exs: Collectively, we raised a thousand dollars.
We are collectively richer than ever.

src.t: And clearly since we are all collectively far, far wealthier than we were in hunter-gatherer times, wealth creation is positive.
src.zh: 很明显，和狩猎采集时代相比，我们所有人加起来拥有的财富已经多得多了。这说明财富是可以被创造出来的。

cards.ex: Limited means there's only a certain amount, not unlimited.
exs: Seats are limited.
I have limited time today.

src.t: But status is limited.
src.zh: 但地位是有限的。

cards.ex: To be enough for everyone who needs or wants some.
exs: Is there enough cake to go around?
There's limited status to go around.

src.t: There’s limited status to go around.
src.zh: 地位就那么多，不够大家分。

cards.note: go around 在这里是“够大家分”，不是“到处走”。

cards.ex: A ranking is a list that shows who is first, second and so on.
exs: Our salon's ranking went up on Google.
Don't obsess over rankings.

src.t: It’s a ranking ladder, it’s a hierarchy, and so if one person rises in status, somebody else has to lower in status.
src.zh: 地位就像一张排名表，有高有低。所以一个人的排名往上升，就意味着另一个人的相对排名要下降。

cards.ex: A ladder is something you climb with steps. A social ladder is a ranking of who's higher.
exs: He climbed the career ladder fast.
Hold the ladder for me.

src.t: It’s a ranking ladder, it’s a hierarchy, and so if one person rises in status, somebody else has to lower in status.

lg: 一级一级往上爬的梯子。

cards.ex: A system in which people or groups are placed at different levels of power or importance.

src.t: It’s a ranking ladder, it’s a hierarchy, and so if one person rises in status, somebody else has to lower in status.

cards.ex: Multiple means more than one, many.

src.t: Now you can have multiple kinds of status, so you can expand some kinds of status,

cards.ex: In a way that is part of the basic nature of something, not just caused by the situation.
exs: Change is inherently uncomfortable.

src.t: Just realize the status games are inherently limited.
src.zh: 只要意识到，地位游戏天生就是有限的。

cards.ex: Quick to argue, fight, or compete against others.
exs: He gets combative when he's tired.

src.t: They’re always combative.
src.zh: 它们总是带着对抗性。

cards.ex: To require means to need something.
exs: This style requires two hours.

cards.ex: To succeed means to do what you were trying to do.
exs: Her studio succeeded in its first year.
If at first you don't succeed, try again.

src.t: Yes, in the marketplace your product has to succeed,

cards.ex: To give reasons for an opinion; it can also mean to disagree or fight with words.
exs: I'd argue that rest is part of work.

src.t: So I would argue that wealth creation games are both more pleasant, they’re positive-sum, and they actually have concrete material returns.
src.zh: 所以我认为，创造财富不仅更让人愉快，而且能让整体的财富增加，还能带来实实在在的物质回报。

cards.ex: To exchange means to give one thing and get another thing back.
exs: Can I exchange this for a different size?

src.t: Show me where you can exchange your status at the bank.
src.zh: 你倒是说说看，哪家银行能让你把社会地位直接换成钱？

lg: 你给我这个，我给你那个。

cards.ex: Not clear or exact enough to understand well.
exs: Her answer was vague.
I have a vague memory of it.

src.t: Exactly, it’s vague and fuzzy.
src.zh: 没错，它模糊又说不清。

cards.ex: Not clear or sharply defined; in this conversation, hard to measure or explain.
exs: The photo is fuzzy.
My memory is a bit fuzzy.

src.t: Exactly, it’s vague and fuzzy.
src.zh: 没错，它模糊又说不清。

cards.ex: To get rich means to become wealthy.
exs: He wants to get rich quickly.
Few people get rich overnight.

src.t: Now, you see people get rich, they have money, what do they want?
src.zh: 你看，人们变富了，有钱了，他们想要什么？

cards.ex: To star in a movie means to play one of the main roles in it.
exs: She starred in a hit movie.

src.t: They want status, so they go to Hollywood, start starring in movies, they donate to non-profits, they go to Cannes or Davos, and they start trying to trade the money for status.

src.zh: 他们有了钱，又想获得社会地位，于是去好莱坞演电影、给非营利组织捐款、出入戛纳和达沃斯，试着拿钱换名望。

cards.ex: Organizations whose main purpose is not to pay profits to owners; many work for public or social goals.
exs: She works for a non-profit.
Rich people often donate to non-profits.

src.t: They want status, so they go to Hollywood, start starring in movies, they donate to non-profits, they go to Cannes or Davos, and they start trying to trade the money for status.
src.zh: 他们有了钱，又想获得社会地位，于是去好莱坞演电影、给非营利组织捐款、出入戛纳和达沃斯，试着拿钱换名望。

lg: 不为赚钱、只为帮人的组织。
cards.note: 非营利不等于“完全不赚钱”，而是主要目标不是向所有者分配利润；可以有收入、员工和运营成本。

cards.ex: To trade means to give one thing to get another.
exs: They trade money for status.
Want to trade seats?

src.t: They want status, so they go to Hollywood, start starring in movies, they donate to non-profits, they go to Cannes or Davos, and they start trying to trade the money for status.

cards.ex: In a way that relates to how humans or other living things developed over many generations.
exs: Evolutionarily, we fear snakes.
We're evolutionarily built to want status.

src.t: People always want what they don’t have, and we are evolutionarily hardwired for status because as I said, wealth creation didn’t really exist until the agricultural revolution when you could store grain.
src.zh: 人总想得到自己还没有的东西。而我们对地位的渴望，是漫长进化过程中形成的；因为就像我说的，直到农业革命让人能储存粮食，创造财富这件事才真正开始出现。

lg: 从猴子到人的漫长路上形成的。

cards.ex: So deeply built into how someone thinks or reacts that it feels automatic; not necessarily impossible to change.
exs: Babies are hardwired to recognize faces.

src.t: People always want what they don’t have, and we are evolutionarily hardwired for status because as I said, wealth creation didn’t really exist until the agricultural revolution when you could store grain.

lg: 线路焊死在里面，改不了。
cards.note: hardwired 是比喻，指本能倾向很强，不代表完全不能改变。

cards.ex: The agricultural revolution was when humans started farming instead of only hunting and gathering.
exs: The agricultural revolution changed everything.
Cities began after the agricultural revolution.

lg: 人类开始种地的大转变。

cards.ex: Grain is the seeds of plants like wheat and rice that we eat.
exs: They stored grain for winter.
Rice is a grain.

cards.zh: 把它提升到另一个层次
cards.ex: To take something to another level means to make it much bigger or better.
exs: Her new studio takes it to another level.
Practice takes your skills to another level.

src.t: Then the industrial revolution took it to another level and now the information age is taking it to yet another level.
src.zh: 后来工业革命把它提升到了另一个层次，现在信息时代又把它推向了更高的层次。

cards.ex: The information age is our time, when computers and the internet are central to life and work.
exs: In the information age, anyone can learn online.
The information age changed jobs.

src.t: Then the industrial revolution took it to another level and now the information age is taking it to yet another level.
src.zh: 后来工业革命把它提升到了另一个层次，现在信息时代又把它推向了更高的层次。

lg: 人人手里拿着网络的时代。

cards.ex: To make money means to earn money.
exs: I make money doing lashes.
You can make money online.

src.t: There’s never been an easier time to make money.
src.zh: 赚钱从来没有像现在这么容易过。

cards.ex: Something that helps you get a bigger result from the same amount of effort, such as software, money, or media.
exs: Social media gives small businesses leverage.
Use your skills as leverage.

src.t: Yes, it’s still hard, but there’s never been an easier time to create wealth, because there’s so much leverage out there, there’s so much opportunity.
src.zh: 没错，创造财富仍然不容易，但现在比过去任何时候都更有机会，因为有太多能放大个人努力的工具，也有太多机会。

lg: 一根撬棍，小力气撬大石头。
cards.note: leverage 的画面是用杠杆放大力量；这里是技术、资本、媒体带来的放大效应。

cards.ex: An opportunity is a good chance to do something.
exs: This is a great opportunity.
Don't miss the opportunity.

src.t: Yes, it’s still hard, but there’s never been an easier time to create wealth, because there’s so much leverage out there, there’s so much opportunity.
src.zh: 没错，创造财富仍然不容易，但现在比过去任何时候都更有机会，因为有太多能放大个人努力的工具，也有太多机会。

cards.ex: To receive something good without having to work or plan for it.
exs: Clients won't just fall on your lap.
Success rarely falls into your lap.

src.t: You still have to go find it, it’s not easy, it’s not gonna fall on your lap and you have to learn something and know something and do something interesting,
src.ft: You still have to go find it, it’s not easy, it’s not gonna fall on your lap and you have to learn something and know something and do something interesting, but nevertheless it’s possible to many more people.
src.zh: 你还是得自己去找，这不容易，机会不会自己掉到你怀里，你得学点东西、懂点东西、做点有意思的事，但即便如此，今天还是有比过去多得多的人有机会做到。

cards.note: 原文固定说法为 fall on your lap；另有常见说法 fall into your lap，不能因此修改采访原文。 原文用 `fall on your lap`，应原样保留；可以在教学注释中告诉学习者 `fall into your lap` 也是常见搭配。

cards.ex: Despite that; even though the previous point is true.
exs: It was hard. Nevertheless, we finished.
She was tired; nevertheless, she smiled.

src.t: but nevertheless it’s possible to many more people.
src.ft: You still have to go find it, it’s not easy, it’s not gonna fall on your lap and you have to learn something and know something and do something interesting, but nevertheless it’s possible to many more people.

cards.ex: A serf was a poor farm worker in the past who had to work the land for a lord and wasn't free.
exs: Serfs couldn't leave the land.
Born a serf, die a serf.

src.t: A few hundred years ago you were born a serf, you were gonna die a serf, there was almost no way out of that.
src.zh: 几百年前，你生来是农奴，死的时候也还是农奴，几乎没有出路。

lg: 一辈子给地主种地的人。

src.t: That’s changed, and so I would argue that you’re better off focusing on wealth games than status games.
src.zh: 时代已经变了。所以我的建议是，与其把精力放在争地位上，不如放在创造财富上。

cards.ex: To build up means to make something bigger or stronger over time.
exs: She built up a big client list.

src.t: If you’re trying to build up, for example, your following on a social network and get famous and then get rich off of being famous,
src.ft: If you’re trying to build up, for example, your following on a social network and get famous and then get rich off of being famous, that’s a much harder path than getting rich first, and then go for your fame afterwards would be my advice.

exs: As you said, it's a busy week.
As you said, timing matters.

src.t: A lot of people do that, as you said.
src.zh: 正如你说的，很多人都这么做。

src.t: It’s funny how people who have achieved such a level of wealth – you think why do you need the status, given that most people use status to then try and cash in to achieve wealth?
src.zh: 有意思的是，有些人明明已经非常有钱了，你就会想：既然大多数人都是先争取名望、再把名望变成财富，那这些人为什么还要追求地位呢？

lg: 把这个事实摆在桌上考虑。

cards.note: cash in 侧重利用已有机会或名气获得收益；cash in on something 更明确。

cards.ex: Enough money to be able to say no to work or demands you do not want. Strong, rude slang.

src.zh: 如果你已经有足够的钱，可以不看任何人的脸色；如果你已经过了需要为钱奔波的阶段，或者手里有很多资产，为什么还要反过来追逐地位呢？

lg: 多到可以对谁都说不的钱（粗口）。
cards.note: 粗口表达强调有选择权、能拒绝不合理要求；不是字面骂人，正式场合慎用。 粗口；解释为“财务上有足够底气拒绝不想做的事”，避免教成日常礼貌用语。

cards.ex: Owning a lot of valuable assets; it does not always mean having a lot of cash available.

cards.zh: 玩这个游戏；按规则参与
cards.ex: To play the game means to take part in something by its rules.
exs: You have to play the game to win.
Why play the game at all?

src.t: Does that mean the reason to play the game is to win the game and be done with it?
src.zh: 你的意思是，我们参与这场游戏，就是为了赢下来，然后不再被它牵着走吗？

cards.ex: To have finished with something and no longer want or need to deal with it.
exs: I'm done with that diet.
Win it and be done with it.

src.t: Is it harder to win and be done with for status than it is for wealth?
src.zh: 相比财富，要在地位竞争中赢到一个可以停下来的程度，是不是更难？

src.t: That’s a good observation, I hadn’t thought that through, but you’re right.
src.zh: 这个观察很到位，我之前没想透，但你说得对。

cards.ex: To consider a problem carefully, including what might happen next.

src.zh: 这个观察很到位，我之前没想透，但你说得对。

src.zh: 我觉得人们永远会想要更多地位，但财富到了一定程度，你是可以满足的。

exs: He climbed the ladder quickly at work.
It's hard to climb that ladder.

src.t: That one’s harder to climb the ladder on,
src.ft: That one’s harder to climb the ladder on, but the fact that, for example, iTunes and YouTube can put you in competition against your contemporaries every single day, and make you go up and down and show you likes and comments and ratings.
src.zh: 在那个榜单上想往上爬就更难了，可问题是，像 iTunes 和 YouTube 这样的平台，每天都能让你跟同行比高低，让排名不断升降，还不断给你看点赞、评论和评分。

cards.ex: Competition is when people try to beat each other.
exs: There's a lot of competition in my area.
Healthy competition helps.

src.t: but the fact that, for example, iTunes and YouTube can put you in competition against your contemporaries every single day, and make you go up and down and show you likes and comments and ratings.

cards.ex: People who live or work during the same period as you, especially in the same field.
exs: She's more successful than her contemporaries.
He competes with his contemporaries.

src.t: but the fact that, for example, iTunes and YouTube can put you in competition against your contemporaries every single day, and make you go up and down and show you likes and comments and ratings.
src.ft: That one’s harder to climb the ladder on, but the fact that, for example, iTunes and YouTube can put you in competition against your contemporaries every single day, and make you go up and down and show you likes and comments and ratings.
src.zh: 在那个榜单上想往上爬就更难了，可问题是，像 iTunes 和 YouTube 这样的平台，每天都能让你跟同行比高低，让排名不断升降，还不断给你看点赞、评论和评分。

cards.ex: A machine you run on without moving forward; also a repeated activity that keeps you busy without making you feel finished.
exs: I run on the treadmill at the gym.
Social media is a treadmill.

src.t: They’ll keep you running on that treadmill forever.
src.zh: 它们会让你一直困在这种永远跑不完的竞争里。

cards.note: 跑步机比喻：不停努力追逐排名，却永远没有“完成”的那一刻。

cards.ex: The direction something is moving or developing over time.
exs: Her career is on a great trajectory.
Trajectory matters more than position.

src.t: Jimmy Carr has this cool idea where he says trajectory is more important than position.
src.zh: Jimmy Carr 有个很有意思的观点：比起你现在排在哪里，更重要的是你正在往哪个方向走。

lg: 往哪个方向飞的那条线。
cards.note: position 是此刻在哪里，trajectory 是一段时间里往哪里发展。

cards.ex: A position is a place or rank.
exs: What's your position in the ranking?
He's in a good position.

src.t: Jimmy Carr has this cool idea where he says trajectory is more important than position.
src.zh: Jimmy Carr 有个很有意思的观点：比起你现在排在哪里，更重要的是你正在往哪个方向走。

lg: 你当时站在哪里、处在什么处境

cards.ex: Versus means compared to or against.
exs: Coffee versus tea, which do you like?
Quality versus quantity.

src.t: versus you’re number two in the world, but last year you were number one, there is this sense of the deceleration is very, very tangible.
src.ft: So, if you are number one hundred and one in the world, but last year you were number two hundred, versus you’re number two in the world, but last year you were number one, there is this sense of the deceleration is very, very tangible.
src.zh: 比如，如果你现在世界排名第一百零一，但去年排第两百，而另一个人虽然排世界第二，去年却是第一。即使排名仍然很高，那种自己正在往下掉的感觉也会非常强烈。

cards.ex: The act of becoming slower; in this talk, the feeling that your progress is losing speed.
exs: The car's deceleration was smooth.
People feel deceleration strongly.

src.t: versus you’re number two in the world, but last year you were number one, there is this sense of the deceleration is very, very tangible.
src.ft: So, if you are number one hundred and one in the world, but last year you were number two hundred, versus you’re number two in the world, but last year you were number one, there is this sense of the deceleration is very, very tangible.
src.zh: 比如，如果你现在世界排名第一百零一，但去年排第两百，而另一个人虽然排世界第二，去年却是第一。即使排名仍然很高，那种自己正在往下掉的感觉也会非常强烈。

cards.note: deceleration 严格指速度变慢；排名下降不必然等于“减速”，此处是说失去上升势头的感受。 核心是“减速”，不直接等同“排名下跌”；原句把名次对比和下滑感放在一起。

cards.ex: Real enough to be clearly felt, noticed, or measured.
exs: We saw tangible results.
The tension was tangible.

src.t: versus you’re number two in the world, but last year you were number one, there is this sense of the deceleration is very, very tangible.

src.zh: 比如，如果你现在世界排名第一百零一，但去年排第两百，而另一个人虽然排世界第二，去年却是第一。即使排名仍然很高，那种自己正在往下掉的感觉也会非常强烈。

cards.ex: Evolution is how living things slowly change over many generations.
exs: Evolution shaped our brains.
It goes back to evolution.

src.t: And again it goes back to evolution.
src.zh: 这又回到了进化。

lg: 一代代慢慢变出来的样子。

cards.ex: Losing blood; it can also describe a continuing loss of money or other resources.
exs: My finger is bleeding.
The business is bleeding money.

src.t: Something that is bleeding eventually dies, unless you stop the bleeding, so you’re hardwired not to lose what you have.
src.zh: 一个生命如果一直失血，最终就会死，除非及时止血。所以从本能上，我们特别害怕失去已经拥有的东西。

cards.ex: Eventually means in the end, after a long time.
exs: Eventually, she opened her own studio.
It will work out eventually.

src.t: Something that is bleeding eventually dies, unless you stop the bleeding, so you’re hardwired not to lose what you have.
src.zh: 一个生命如果一直失血，最终就会死，除非及时止血。所以从本能上，我们特别害怕失去已经拥有的东西。

cards.ex: Except if; used to say what must happen to prevent a result.
exs: I'll go unless it rains.
You won't improve unless you practice.

src.t: Something that is bleeding eventually dies, unless you stop the bleeding, so you’re hardwired not to lose what you have.
src.zh: 一个生命如果一直失血，最终就会死，除非及时止血。所以从本能上，我们特别害怕失去已经拥有的东西。

cards.note: unless = if ... not（在很多句子里可这样理解），先找“除非”对应的例外条件。

cards.ex: To evolve means to change and develop slowly over time.
exs: Humans evolved over millions of years.
My style evolved a lot.

src.t: Because we evolved in conditions where we’re so close to just not surviving, you don’t want to give anything up.
src.zh: 因为我们是在差一点就活不下去的条件下进化来的，所以你什么都不想放弃。

lg: 慢慢长成了现在的样子。

cards.ex: Conditions are the situation or environment around you.
exs: Working conditions here are good.
We evolved in harsh conditions.

src.t: Because we evolved in conditions where we’re so close to just not surviving, you don’t want to give anything up.
src.zh: 因为我们是在差一点就活不下去的条件下进化来的，所以你什么都不想放弃。

cards.ex: To stop doing something or let go of something you have.
exs: I don't want to give anything up.
She gave up sugar.

src.t: Because we evolved in conditions where we’re so close to just not surviving, you don’t want to give anything up.
src.zh: 因为我们是在差一点就活不下去的条件下进化来的，所以你什么都不想放弃。

cards.ex: To grip means to hold something very tightly.
exs: Grip the tweezers lightly.
He gripped the handle.

src.t: So you grip tightly?
src.zh: 所以你会紧紧抓住不放？

cards.ex: Tightly means firmly and closely, with no space.
exs: Hold my hand tightly.
Close the lid tightly.

src.t: So you grip tightly?
src.zh: 所以你会紧紧抓住不放？

cards.zh: 物质回报；实实在在的收益
cards.ex: Real benefits you can receive, especially money or useful things.
exs: Good work brings material returns.
Lash training gave me real material returns.
cards.note: material 是物质上的，returns 是回报；一起指可落地的收益。

src.t: So I would argue that wealth creation games are both more pleasant, they’re positive-sum, and they actually have concrete material returns.
src.zh: 所以我认为，创造财富不仅更让人愉快，而且能让整体的财富增加，还能带来实实在在的物质回报。

cards.zh: （财务上）已经不用再为钱奔波的
cards.ex: No longer mainly focused on earning money, often because you already have enough.
exs: After selling his company, he was post-money.
Post-money people often look for status.
cards.note: 在此语境中指“已经不必把赚钱当首要目标”；不是固定标准金融术语。

src.t: If you’ve achieved “fuck you money” already, if you’re post-money or asset-heavy as it’s known, why are you trying to go in the other direction?
src.zh: 如果你已经有足够的钱，可以不看任何人的脸色；如果你已经过了需要为钱奔波的阶段，或者手里有很多资产，为什么还要反过来追逐地位呢？

lg: 钱这关已经过了，站在“钱之后”。

cards.ex: To let something take less of your attention than before.
exs: I get less distracted by my phone at work now.
Try to get less distracted by other people's opinions.
cards.note: get + 比较级形容词 = 逐渐变得不那么……；by 指造成分心的事物。

src.t: There’s a real draw of being swayed by social approval, but how should people learn to get less distracted by status games in that way?
src.zh: 得到别人的认可确实很有吸引力，也很容易让人受它左右。但人们该怎么学着不那么容易被这种地位竞争分散注意力呢？

lg: 注意力被拉走得越来越少。

cards.w: as much as they used to
cards.ex: To the same degree as in the past.
exs: Prices don't change as much as they used to.
My clients don't call as much as they used to.
cards.note: 和过去相比的程度；否定时“不再像以前那么……”。

src.t: I think it just helps to see that status games don’t matter as much as they used to.
src.zh: 我觉得，看清地位游戏已经不像过去那么重要，会很有帮助。

lg: 拿现在和过去比一比程度。

cards.ex: To use a situation or success to get money or another benefit.
exs: She cashed in on the lash trend.
Some people cash in on their fame.
cards.note: 和原文 cash in 相关的常用拓展；注意原文没有 on，不能往原文里加。 原文是 cash in to achieve wealth，没有 on；cash in on + 机会/名气 是常用拓展说法，不能往原文里加 on。

src.t: It’s funny how people who have achieved such a level of wealth – you think why do you need the status, given that most people use status to then try and cash in to achieve wealth?
src.zh: 有意思的是，有些人明明已经非常有钱了，你就会想：既然大多数人都是先争取名望、再把名望变成财富，那这些人为什么还要追求地位呢？

lg: 把手里的机会或名气“兑换”成钱。

cards.ex: To have a strong natural tendency to want or do something.
exs: Babies are hardwired for language.
We are hardwired for connection.
cards.note: for 后接渴望/倾向的目标，如 status；不是完全无法改变。

src.t: People always want what they don’t have, and we are evolutionarily hardwired for status because as I said, wealth creation didn’t really exist until the agricultural revolution when you could store grain.
src.zh: 人总想得到自己还没有的东西。而我们对地位的渴望，是漫长进化过程中形成的；因为就像我说的，直到农业革命让人能储存粮食，创造财富这件事才真正开始出现。

lg: 像电线焊死在大脑里，自动就想要。

cards.ex: A habit of comparing yourself with others that makes you feel you are never good enough.
exs: Social media is a comparison trap.
I try not to fall into the comparison trap.
cards.note: 现有 comparison 和 Chunk 相关；若已经作为独立词卡存在就跳过。

src.t: Satisfaction games, the allure of accruing, whether it’s fame, actual fame, or just the competition comparison trap, it’s always there.
src.zh: 人总会被不断积累东西的诱惑吸引——不管是名气、真正的知名度，还是陷入竞争和攀比的圈套。这种诱惑始终都在。

lg: 一比较就掉进去、总觉得自己不够好的坑。

cards.ex: Subscribers are people who sign up to follow a channel or get updates.
exs: Her channel has ten thousand subscribers.
Thanks to all my subscribers.
cards.note: 原文本句的原声里没有 subscribers（文字按原声），这张卡作为拓展词保留，可联系 R56 的 likes / comments / ratings。
